Key Viva & Interview Questions (Short & Clear Answers)

Q: What is patient deterioration and why is recall critical?

A: Patient deterioration is the acute decline in bodily function (e.g., from sepsis or shock). Recall measures how many deteriorating patients the model catches. A false negative means a dying patient is called 'stable' and missed, leading to death. Therefore, high recall is vital to ensure patient safety.

Q: Why did Random Forest outperform Logistic Regression?

A: Human physiology deteriorates non-linearly. A high heart rate of 120 bpm combined with low blood pressure (85 mmHg) and fast breathing (26 breaths/min) indicates septic shock. Random Forest uses 120 decision trees to capture multi-parameter interactions, whereas Logistic Regression only fits a flat linear hyper-plane (getting only 0.6437 ROC-AUC).

Q: What was the dataset used and how did you prevent data leakage?

A: We used the PhysioNet Challenge 2019 ICU dataset (38,809 raw records). We created a matched 1:1 clinical case-control cohort of 1,586 records. Data leakage was prevented by splitting data into 80% train and 20% test before fitting Scikit-Learn pipelines, ensuring median imputers and scalers were fit strictly on training data.

Q: What are the top features driving deterioration?

A: Based on Random Forest Gini feature importances: Age (23.2%), Heart Rate (20.3%), and Respiratory Rate (14.8%) are the top three drivers of acute clinical decompensation.

Academic Project Report Summary

Problem Statement: Hospitals continuously monitor patient vital signs, but manually identifying early deterioration can be difficult. This project compares machine learning classification algorithms for early prediction of patient deterioration using routine bedside vitals.

Best Model: Random Forest Classifier achieved 70.44% Accuracy, 67.30% Recall, 69.48% F1-score, and 0.7868 ROC-AUC, outperforming KNN, SVM, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression.

Deployment: The full project contains an interactive Streamlit application (app.py) and a 1-click batch launcher (START_APPLICATION.bat) inside patient-deterioration-early-warning.zip.

Medical Disclaimer: This application is an academic machine-learning study designed solely for educational evaluation and technical research. It does NOT constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or clinical guidance. It must not be deployed in real patient care settings without formal clinical trials and regulatory certification.
